item.title: 2003: Josh Beckett Pitches Five-Hit Shutout as Marlins Win World Series
item.description: In Game 6 of the World Series at Yankee Stadium, Josh Beckett, on three days' rest, pitches a 2–0, five-hit shutout over the favored New York Yankees, to give the Florida Marlins their second championship in 11 seasons. Beckett receives Series MVP honors. Photo: User PhreddieH3 on en.wikipedia (Public domain).

item.title: 2021: Phillies Hire Dickerson as Infield Coach
item.description: On October 25, 2021, the Phillies hired Dickerson as their infield coach. Photo: Ryan Casey Aguinaldo (CC BY-SA 4.0).

item.title: 2018: Blue Jays Hire Montoyo as Manager, Replacing John Gibbons
item.description: On October 25, 2018, Montoyo was hired by the Toronto Blue Jays as their new manager, replacing John Gibbons. Photo: Keith Allison from Hanover, MD, USA (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2017: Astros Beat Dodgers 7-6 in 11 Innings, Tie World Series
item.description: The Houston Astros beat the host Los Angeles Dodgers, 7–6, in 11 innings in Game 2 to tie the World Series. Photo: Christopher Okula (Original version) UCinternational (Crop) (Public domain).

item.title: 2011: Cubs Introduce Theo Epstein as New President
item.description: The Chicago Cubs introduce former Boston Red Sox general manager Theo Epstein as their new president, while the Red Sox name Ben Cherington the team's executive vice president/general manager. Photo: Scott Slingsby from Rochester, NH (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2010: Blue Jays Formally Introduce Farrell as 2011 Manager
item.description: The Blue Jays held a press conference on October 25, 2010, formally introducing Farrell as the team's manager for the 2011 season. Photo: Keith Allison from Owings Mills, USA (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2009: Yankees Beat Angels 5-2, Win 40th AL Pennant in Game 6
item.description: The New York Yankees win their 40th American League pennant (and the first in six years) beating the Los Angeles Angels, 5–2, in Game 6 of the ALCS. Andy Pettitte earns his 16th postseason victory, breaking a tie with John Smoltz for most wins in the postseason. CC Sabathia is selected MVP of the series. Photo: jcasabona (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2008: Albert Pujols Named 2008 Winner of Roberto Clemente Award
item.description: Albert Pujols of the Cardinals is named the 2008 winner of the Roberto Clemente Award. He is also named Players Choice Player of the Year for the second time, having also won in 2003, the Player's Choice Award's NL Outstanding Player and The Sporting News Major League Player of the Year. Photo: shgmom56 (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2006: Edward F. Kenney, 85, Red Sox Farm System Executive
item.description: Edward F. Kenney, 85, who served as a Boston Red Sox farm system executive for over 40 years.

item.title: 2005: Blum's Two-out Homer Gives White Sox 14-Inning Win
item.description: In the first World Series game played in the state of Texas, former Astro Geoff Blum wins the longest game in WS history with a tiebreaking two-out solo home run as the Chicago White Sox beat the Houston Astros 7–5 at Minute Maid Park to move within a win of a sweep and their first title since 1917. The 14-inning marathon lasts a total of five hours and 41 minutes. Photo: William Holtkamp on Flickr (Original version) User UCinternational (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 1988: La Russa Wins AL Manager of the Year Over Morgan
item.description: With 15 of 28 first place votes and 103 points, Tony La Russa of the Oakland Athletics is elected AL Manager of the Year by the Baseball Writers' Association of America; Joe Morgan, who took control of the Boston Red Sox on July 14, is the runner-up (nine first-place mentions, 89 points). Photo: Gage Skidmore (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 1987: Viola, Reardon Hold Cardinals to Six Hits, Twins Win Game 7
item.description: In Game 7 of the World Series, starter Frank Viola and reliever Jeff Reardon hold the St. Louis Cardinals to six hits, as the Minnesota Twins win 4–2 for their first Fall Classic championship in their 27-year history in the Twin Cities. The franchise's last title came in 1924 as the Washington Senators. Viola is named the Series MVP. Photo: Jon Gudorf Photography (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 1986: Red Sox Lead 5-3, One out From First Title Since 1918
item.description: Leading 5–3 in Game 6 of the World Series, and just one out away from winning their first championship since 1918, the Red Sox surrender singles to Gary Carter, Kevin Mitchell and Ray Knight, and pitcher Bob Stanley throws a wild pitch that allows Mitchell to tie the game. Photo: Craig Johnson from San Diego, CA, USA (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 1976: Claire Merritt Ruth, 79, Widow of Babe Ruth
item.description: Claire Merritt Ruth, 79, widow of Babe Ruth, who died on August 16, 1948

item.title: 1972: Pirates Trade Gene Garber to Royals for Jim Rooker
item.description: The Pirates make a consequential trade, obtaining left-hander Jim Rooker from the Kansas City Royals for reliever Gene Garber. Rooker, 30, will spend eight seasons as a Pirate, and win 82 games for them.

item.title: 1967: Astros Sign César Cedeño, 16, as International Free Agent
item.description: The Houston Astros sign outfielder César Cedeño, 16, as an international free agent.

item.title: 1965: Leo Durocher, 60, Returns as Cubs Manager, Ends College of Coaches
item.description: After a decade's hiatus, Leo Durocher, 60, resumes his managerial career when he is appointed to lead the 1966 Chicago Cubs. At his press conference with owner Philip K. Wrigley, Durocher emphatically ends the Cubs' "College of Coaches" experiment when he declares, "I'm not a 'head coach.' I'm the manager."

item.title: 1960: Gabe Paul Quits Reds to Become Houston's Expansion Front-Office Boss
item.description: Gabe Paul, general manager of the Cincinnati Reds since October 1951, quits his post to join Houston's National League expansion team as their first front-office boss. Although Paul doesn't stay long, he brings young Cincinnati executives Tal Smith and Bill Giles to Houston, and both play key roles in what will become the Colt .45s/Astros' early years. Photo: Producer: New York Yankees & MLB (Public domain).

item.title: 1956: Marty Marion Resigns as White Sox Manager After Third-Place Finish
item.description: Chicago White Sox manager Marty Marion resigns in the wake of a third-place finish and criticism from general manager Chuck Comiskey. Four days later, former Cleveland pilot Al López will replace him; in his third season, López will guide the 1959 White Sox to their first American League flag in 40 years.

item.title: 1943: Branch Rickey Signs Leo Durocher to One-Year Deal for 1944
item.description: The fate of Leo Durocher is decided when Brooklyn Dodgers club president Branch Rickey signs his controversial manager to a one-year contract to return for a sixth season in 1944. Rickey had left the 38-year-old pilot dangling after a disappointing 1943 campaign that saw the Dodgers finish 23½ games behind the St. Louis Cardinals and endure a brief player uprising against Durocher in mid-season. Photo: Conrad Poirier (Public domain).

item.title: 1941: Bill Phillips, 72, Pitcher and 1914 Indianapolis Hoosiers Manager
item.description: Bill Phillips, 72, pitcher for the Pittsburgh Alleghenys and the Cincinnati Reds of the National League in seven seasons between 1890 and 1903, who is best remembered for managing the 1914 Indianapolis Hoosiers to the Federal League pennant. Photo: Bain News Service, publisher (Public domain).

item.title: 1917: Yankees Sign Miller Huggins to Two-Year Contract, Replacing Donovan
item.description: The Yankees and the owners, Jacob Ruppert and Tillinghast L'Hommedieu Huston, announced on October 25, 1917 that they had signed Miller Huggins to a two year contract that paid around $12,000 (1917 USD) per season, replacing Bill Donovan.

item.title: 1904: Cornelius Van Cott, 66, Former New York Giants Owner
item.description: Cornelius Van Cott, 66, owner of the New York Giants from January 1893 to January 1895.

item.title: 1888: Giants Clinch Series With 11-3 Win Over St. Louis Browns
item.description: The New York Giants clinch the series with an 11–3 win over the St. Louis Browns. The final 2 games will be played for revenue purposes with St. Louis winning both contests for an overall series result of 6 games to 4 in favor of the Giants. (World Series results are also recorded for 1889.) Photo: Goodwin & Company (Public domain).

item.title: 1884: Providence Sweeps Metropolitans 12-2, Radbourn Wins All Three
item.description: The Providence Grays complete the sweep of the New York Metropolitans with a 12–2 win in a game called after 6 innings because of extreme cold and an attendance of only 300 at the Polo Grounds. Charley Radbourn, after winning 59 games during the regular season, wins all 3 games for Providence while allowing no earned runs. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).
